title: Session-slice heuristic allocator for streaming completions
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Streaming chat completions show highly skewed session lengths and token emission patterns. Current continuous batcher groups by arrival window which reduces GPU utilization under high variance and causes suboptimal KV cache residency for long-running sessions. Goal: Implement a session-slice heuristic allocator that forms micro-batches by slicing long sessions into bounded ‘slices’ and packing short-turn sessions together, while prioritizing KV cache locality and minimizing GPU memory fragmentation. This ticket covers design, simulation, prototype implementation in the allocator, benchmark harnesses, and rollout plan.

Scope:
- Heuristic design and scoring function for session-slices (latency budget, token budget, KV locality score, priority).
- Implement slice creation at the batching ingress and affinity-based packer to map slices to GPU slabs.
- KV cache tagging so slices carry hot-key hints to avoid preemptive eviction of active prefixes.
- Lightweight GPU slab packing algorithm with soft quota enforcement to prevent OOMs and reduce tail-latency spikes.
- Telemetry additions: slice-level traces, per-slab KV-hit metrics, evictions per-turn.
- Benchmarks: synthetic skewed conversational traces and production trace replay.

Out of scope for this ticket: quantization kernel changes, scheduler-level multi-tenant reservations (handled in dedicated capacity), and UI console changes (follow-up PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Latency p50 for streaming completions does not increase by >5% on production trace replay compared to baseline
End-to-end token cost for batch-serving decreases by >=7% on synthetic 70/30 long/short session workload
KV-hit ratio improvement >=10% for long sessions (>=1k tokens) through slice affinity tagging
No increase in OOM events in stress tests; soft quota prevents slab overflow with <1% enforced preemption
Instrumentation emits slice_id, slab_id, kv_tag, and eviction_reason for every batch; dashboards created
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Kickoff with serving runtime and infra. Agreed on target metrics and bumped estimate after design session.

2026-02-25: Drafted scoring formula: score = w_latency*(remaining_latency_budget/req_deadline) + w_tokens*(remaining_token_budget/max_slice_tokens) + w_kv*(kv_hotness_score) + w_gpu*(slab_free_ratio). We will normalize weights per workload profile.

2026-03-01: Simulator v1 completed — reproduces skewed stream where 15% of sessions produce 70% of tokens. Early results show potential 12% KV-hit improvement with aggressive slicing but increases packetization overhead.

2026-03-05: Prototype allocator merged to feature branch with flags: session_slicing=true, kv_affinity_tags=true. Basic telemetry hooks added. Integration tests passing on CI but need heavy-load validation.

2026-03-08: Stress run against replay cluster (100k concurrent sessions) shows reduced tail latency but a 2% increase in per-request CPU on batch ingress due to tag computation — acceptable trade-off.
2026-03-10: Design decision to use soft quota slab packing with background compaction rather than strict global packing to reduce preemption churn. Preparing rollout plan and canary metrics.
comments: Marcus Li (2026-02-26): Proposed an incremental rollout — start with low-traffic region and model family beta. Also suggested adding a per-session decay timestamp to avoid stale KV affinity.
Raisa Gómez (Design, 2026-03-02): Reviewed telemetry wireframes; recommend slice-level flamegraphs to correlate latency vs KV hits. Also suggested a visual for slab fragmentation in Console.
Samir Patel (SRE, 2026-03-06): Noted that GC/eviction pressure under high churn may surface in metrics; requested an automatic fallback that disables slicing for affected slabs.
